report:
## Conclusion

Yes, evidence strongly supports that widespread mask wearing by a large proportion of the population can reduce COVID-19 infections. Multiple studies and systematic reviews converge on this finding:

1. **A large-scale PNAS study** analyzing survey data from over 20 million people across six continents found that population mask wearing notably reduced SARS-CoV-2 transmission, with mean mask-wearing levels corresponding to a **19% decrease in the effective reproduction number (R)**. ([https://www.pnas.org/doi/10.1073/pnas.2119266119](https://www.pnas.org/doi/10.1073/pnas.2119266119))

2. **A 2025 systematic literature review** published in MDPI concluded that "masking policies and mask wearing are beneficial to prevent and reduce the risk of SARS-CoV-2 infections and COVID-19 disease in various real-world settings." ([https://www.mdpi.com/1660-4601/22/10/1590](https://www.mdpi.com/1660-4601/22/10/1590))

3. **A PNAS evidence review** (Howard et al.) synthesized the literature on mask usage and found that face masks reduce transmission, with a WHO-sponsored systematic review by Chu et al. showing "face mask use could result in a large reduction in risk of infection." ([https://www.pnas.org/doi/10.1073/pnas.2014564118](https://www.pnas.org/doi/10.1073/pnas.2014564118))

4. **A recent meta-analysis** found that wearing a face mask is associated with a **reduced risk of COVID-19 infection by 11.8% to 28.5%** after controlling for publication bias. ([https://link.springer.com/content/pdf/10.1007/s41885-025-00185-5.pdf](https://link.springer.com/content/pdf/10.1007/s41885-025-00185-5.pdf))

Additionally, a large randomized trial in Bangladesh found that surgical masks reduced COVID-19 by **35% among people aged 60+** and **9–11% overall** in intervention villages. The evidence consistently shows that higher rates of population mask wearing correlate with lower transmission, with surgical/N95 masks generally outperforming cloth masks. While masks are not perfect barriers and work best alongside other measures like distancing, the body of evidence supports their effectiveness at the population level.
